title: Grocery food is generally nontaxable
summary: Food products for human consumption are generally nontaxable. Freezing or refrigerating food to preserve it does not change that: the result turns on the product and how it is sold, not on how it is stored.

scenarios.title: Basic grocery staples
scenarios.taxableWhen: Tax applies only if the item falls outside the statutory food-product definition or is sold in a taxable prepared-food form.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Qualifying food products for human consumption are nontaxable, including ordinary flour, bread, milk, eggs, meat, produce and similar groceries.
scenarios.inPractice: Classify tax at the point of sale by item and sale condition, not by the category of the inventory.

scenarios.title: Fresh produce sold whole
scenarios.taxableWhen: A produce item can become taxable when prepared and sold in a taxable immediate-consumption context, or when another statutory exclusion applies.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Whole fruits and vegetables sold as grocery food products are generally nontaxable.
scenarios.inPractice: Whole produce sold as grocery is the ordinary case; confirm the sale condition (prepared, cut, or served) before treating it otherwise.

scenarios.title: Frozen food held in natural state
scenarios.taxableWhen: A sale may be taxable if the seller heats the food or sells it as taxable prepared food; freezing alone does not create that result.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Food merely frozen or kept frozen to preserve its natural state remains a food product if it otherwise meets §151.314.
scenarios.inPractice: Freezing for storage is not preparation; classify by what the item is and how it is sold.

scenarios.title: Refrigerated food held in natural state
scenarios.taxableWhen: Tax depends on the product and how it is sold, not on refrigeration itself.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Cold storage to preserve food does not by itself convert grocery food into taxable prepared food.
scenarios.inPractice: Classify the product by its retail form and how it is prepared at the point of sale, not by warehouse temperature.

scenarios.title: Bottled water
scenarios.taxableWhen: Flavored water meeting the soft-drink definition is taxable.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Unflavored, mineral, spring and sparkling water are generally nontaxable food products.
scenarios.inPractice: Classify plain water separately from flavored or sweetened beverages.

scenarios.title: Coffee beans and ground coffee
scenarios.taxableWhen: Coffee sold heated, in a cup/glass, or with a straw is taxable under the grocery guidance; sweetened bottled/canned coffee can also be taxable.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Coffee beans, grounds, pods and unsweetened packaged coffee/tea are generally nontaxable grocery food products.
scenarios.inPractice: Coffee bought for internal use is not resale inventory; distinguish dry coffee goods from brewed or hot service.

scenarios.title: Dietary supplements
scenarios.taxableWhen: Products failing statutory dietary-supplement or food-product requirements may be taxable.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Qualifying dietary supplements, commonly identified by a required Supplement Facts panel or statutory alternative criteria, are nontaxable.
scenarios.inPractice: Use the item's actual label and ingredients; do not classify by marketing name.

title: Prepared food is taxable
summary: Food becomes taxable when it is sold as prepared food: heated by the seller, sold with eating utensils, combined at the store, or sold for immediate consumption. A small sales volume does not create an exception.

scenarios.title: Food heated by the seller
scenarios.taxableWhen: Hot food sold after the seller heats it is generally taxable, subject to statutory details and listed exceptions.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Food sold cold or not heated by the seller may remain a nontaxable food product.
scenarios.inPractice: Applies where the seller heats food, typically a cafe or store counter; plain distribution of unheated product is outside it.

scenarios.title: Prepared food sold in an on-site cafe
scenarios.taxableWhen: Prepared meals and hot food sold by the cafe are taxable even if cafe sales are a very small share of total business.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A product that remains a qualifying grocery food product and is not sold as prepared food may be nontaxable.
scenarios.inPractice: Small cafe volume does not waive tax on taxable sales. Track cafe sales separately from wholesale or distribution activity.

scenarios.title: Cold meals and utensils
scenarios.taxableWhen: Cold food sold with eating utensils, or in the taxable prepared-food setting described in the Comptroller rule, can be taxable.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Cold grocery food sold without eating utensils and not in a taxable restaurant/prepared-food transaction may be nontaxable.
scenarios.inPractice: Use a separate point-of-sale tax code for utensils, meal bundles and cold grab-and-go items.

scenarios.title: Deli or counter food for immediate consumption
scenarios.taxableWhen: Food sold through a deli, lunch counter, restaurant or similar location for immediate consumption is generally taxable.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Packaged grocery food for later consumption may be nontaxable when the statutory food-product definition is met.
scenarios.inPractice: Applies to counter and deli sales for immediate consumption, not to ordinary product movement between businesses.

scenarios.title: Sandwiches
scenarios.taxableWhen: Sandwiches are generally taxable prepared food when sold ready to eat.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Frozen or partially frozen sandwiches requiring customer thawing or heating before eating may remain nontaxable.
scenarios.inPractice: Keep the product's state and any customer preparation step visible in the item master.

scenarios.title: Food combined at the store
scenarios.taxableWhen: Food made at a store by combining two or more food ingredients and sold as one item (such as salad, salsa, hummus or pesto) is generally taxable prepared food.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Uncombined grocery ingredients sold separately generally retain their food-product treatment.
scenarios.inPractice: Relevant to stores and counters that assemble items; a distributor that does not prepare product is generally outside it.

scenarios.title: Bakery goods
scenarios.taxableWhen: Bakery items sold by a nonqualifying grocery operation are taxable if heated by the seller or sold with eating utensils.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Bakery items are generally nontaxable when sold cold without utensils; qualifying bakery locations have a separate rule if over 50% of sales are bakery items for off-premises consumption.
scenarios.inPractice: A store-level classification; do not apply it to goods handled at a distribution facility.

scenarios.title: Coffee brewed for office use
scenarios.taxableWhen: A hot beverage sold or provided in a taxable food-service transaction can be taxable; taxable supplies used to brew it remain taxable purchases.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Dry beans/grounds are generally nontaxable food products; brewing coffee for internal office use does not make the business a food manufacturer.
scenarios.inPractice: Code office coffee separately from resale inventory and from cafe sales; confirm whether purchases are dry coffee, prepared cups, or a service bundle.

title: Candy, soft drinks, snacks and vending are carved out
summary: Some items are taxable even though they are food: candy and gum, soft drinks and other sweetened beverages, individual-size snacks, and items sold through vending machines. Definitions and thresholds decide each case.

scenarios.title: Candy and gum
scenarios.taxableWhen: Candy and gum are taxable even when sold in a grocery store.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Items not meeting the statutory candy definition may qualify as food products.
scenarios.inPractice: Maintain product-level tax categories for candy, sweetened nuts and similar items.

scenarios.title: Soft drinks and sports drinks
scenarios.taxableWhen: Sweetened or flavored beverages that meet the statutory soft-drink definition are taxable.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Qualifying milk or milk-substitute drinks and qualifying beverages with more than 50% fruit or vegetable juice may be nontaxable.
scenarios.inPractice: Use ingredient and label data; the word "beverage" alone is not enough to classify.

scenarios.title: Juice drinks
scenarios.taxableWhen: A beverage containing 50% or less fruit/vegetable juice can be a taxable soft drink, depending on ingredients and form.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Beverages containing more than 50% fruit or vegetable juice may qualify as food products.
scenarios.inPractice: Maintain an ingredient-based rule for blends, punches and juice drinks.

scenarios.title: Individual-size snack foods
scenarios.taxableWhen: Snack items sold in an individual-size portion (under 2.5 ounces or labeled no more than one serving) are generally taxable.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Larger non-individual-size packages and multipacks of separate individual packages may be nontaxable, subject to meal/vending exceptions.
scenarios.inPractice: Relevant at checkout; map package size and serving data to the point-of-sale tax code.

scenarios.title: Food sold through vending machines
scenarios.taxableWhen: Food and beverages sold through vending machines are generally taxable under the Comptroller's grocery guidance.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A different nontaxable retail sale may apply outside the vending-machine context if the food-product definition is met.
scenarios.inPractice: If vending is operated, keep those sales distinct from grocery shelf sales.

title: What counts as manufacturing or processing
summary: Whether an operation is manufacturing or processing is a fact test. Handling steps such as washing, trimming, sorting or waxing qualify only when they are part of a process that meets the legal test; the name of the activity does not decide it.

scenarios.title: Produce ripening operation
scenarios.taxableWhen: The manufacturing exemption is not automatic; a qualifying process must meet §151.318 and Rule 3.300. Ripening may be fact-sensitive because it changes product characteristics.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Ordinary storage, staging or holding without qualifying processing does not establish manufacturing status.
scenarios.inPractice: Treat ripening as fact-sensitive: document the steps, equipment, physical change, operator, product ownership, and the point at which the product is sale-ready.

scenarios.title: Ethylene or controlled-atmosphere ripening
scenarios.taxableWhen: Tax may apply to equipment/supplies unless directly used in qualifying actual processing and the statutory conditions are met.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Qualifying equipment directly used in manufacturing/processing for ultimate sale may be exempt; the label “ripening room” alone does not establish it.
scenarios.inPractice: Tie controlled-atmosphere equipment and controls to the documented ripening process, separate from ordinary cold storage.

scenarios.title: Washing produce
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable if washing is incidental handling/storage and the purchased item does not meet an exemption.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Washing may be part of a qualifying processing operation only when the full activity meets the legal test; washing alone does not establish it.
scenarios.inPractice: Classify routine washing and cleaning as handling unless a documented processing analysis supports otherwise.

scenarios.title: Trimming or removing inedible parts
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable where trimming is incidental preparation/handling after manufacture is complete.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A qualifying processing operation may support exemption for direct-use property when the statutory manufacturing test is met.
scenarios.inPractice: Document whether trimming materially changes the product or only makes it suitable for display.

scenarios.title: Cutting or dicing produce
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable if the activity is retail meal preparation or only incidental handling outside a qualifying manufacturing operation.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Equipment/materials directly used in qualifying food processing for ultimate sale may qualify under the manufacturing exemption.
scenarios.inPractice: Analyze any cutting operation separately from ripening, cold storage, and meal preparation.

scenarios.title: Sorting and grading
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when equipment is used for routine inventory selection, storage or distribution.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A process may qualify only if it satisfies Rule 3.300's manufacturing/processing requirements.
scenarios.inPractice: Sorting and grading to fill orders is not assumed to be manufacturing; keep an activity description and process map.

scenarios.title: Waxing produce
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when waxing is post-production handling or used for storage/display without qualifying process treatment.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A specific material may qualify if used directly in qualifying processing and within the manufacturing statute/rule.
scenarios.inPractice: Track waxing materials separately and document purpose, product stage, and whether the activity changes marketability or physical characteristics.

scenarios.title: Cutting and repackaging only
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when the business only cuts/repackages food without satisfying the manufacturing test; the retail food-product result may still be nontaxable.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Comptroller guidance says food cut up/repackaged or pasteurized, such as produce trays, may remain nontaxable food products at retail.
scenarios.inPractice: Retail food taxability and eligibility for the manufacturing-purchase exemption are separate questions.

scenarios.title: Pasteurization
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable if purchased items are used outside a qualifying process.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Food may remain a nontaxable food product after pasteurization; equipment can qualify only under §151.318's manufacturing test.
scenarios.inPractice: Do not use a downstream retail exemption as proof that equipment or inputs are exempt.

scenarios.title: Product made more marketable
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when a purchase supports sales or distribution but is not itself part of a qualifying manufacturing activity.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Qualifying manufacturers may obtain certain chemicals/materials used to make product more marketable under Comptroller guidance.
scenarios.inPractice: Marketing improvement alone does not make a distributor a manufacturer; assess the actual process and material separately.

title: Who qualifies, and where the process starts and ends
summary: The exemption follows the entity and the stage. It covers a qualifying operation producing property for ultimate sale, begins with the first activity that changes the materials, and ends when the product has its final physical properties. An affiliate's or a customer's status does not extend it.

scenarios.title: Packaging stage and product completion
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable for property used after the manufacturing process ends in storage, maintenance or distribution.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Qualifying manufacturer packaging may be within the process; Comptroller says manufacturing ends when the product has the physical properties (including packaging) in which transferred.
scenarios.inPractice: Document when the product is sale-ready and whether packaging is part of completion or of later distribution.

scenarios.title: First production activity
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable for general pre-production/storage activity before qualifying manufacturing begins.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Direct-use items may qualify beginning with the first activity that changes raw materials/ingredients in a qualifying manufacturing process.
scenarios.inPractice: Identify when the physical process starts; receiving and staging alone are not enough.

scenarios.title: Intermediate products
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable for property not used in actual qualifying production.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Direct-use property may qualify if it changes an intermediate/preliminary product that becomes an ingredient or component of the product for sale.
scenarios.inPractice: Use only if an intermediate product is actually created; ordinary custody of produce does not qualify by itself.

scenarios.title: Food for ultimate sale
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable if the operation is not actually producing tangible personal property for sale or property is used for business purposes.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Manufacturing exemptions apply to qualifying manufacture/fabrication/processing for ultimate sale.
scenarios.inPractice: Goods held for sale are the required destination, but the processing activity must still meet the test.

scenarios.title: Separate legal affiliate owns the equipment
scenarios.taxableWhen: Tax follows the taxpayer that purchases/uses the property and the activity it conducts; group membership alone does not extend another affiliate's status.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: An entity can qualify based on its own actual manufacturing/processing activity for sale.
scenarios.inPractice: Identify the equipment owner, operator, inventory owner and purchaser on each invoice; align the exemption claim to the entity performing the process.

scenarios.title: Contract processing for another entity
scenarios.taxableWhen: A service provider that only stores or handles goods does not qualify solely because its customer is a manufacturer.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A submanufacturer actually performing qualifying operations may qualify for the exemption in its own right.
scenarios.inPractice: Determine whether the business performs the physical process or only provides logistics or custody for an affiliate or customer.

scenarios.title: Quality-control testing
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable for general inspection or post-production inventory checks not used in qualifying manufacturing.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Testing products for ultimate sale during the manufacturing operation may qualify under Comptroller guidance.
scenarios.inPractice: Separate production-line food-safety testing from receiving and order-accuracy checks.

title: Storage and refrigeration are not processing
summary: Refrigeration and freezing used only to preserve or store finished goods are not manufacturing. Equipment qualifies only to the extent it is directly used in actual qualifying processing.

scenarios.title: Refrigeration used only to preserve inventory
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when refrigeration equipment or service is used to store completed products or general warehouse inventory.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A specific item may qualify if directly used in actual processing; refrigeration by itself does not establish manufacturing.
scenarios.inPractice: Treat refrigeration for preservation as storage unless evidence shows direct use in processing.

scenarios.title: Freezing to preserve natural state
scenarios.taxableWhen: Freezing solely for preservation/storage is not enough to claim manufacturing treatment.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A process that actually changes product form for sale may require separate analysis under the manufacturing rule.
scenarios.inPractice: Do not conflate holding product frozen with processing it into a new product.

scenarios.title: Refrigeration equipment
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when used to maintain/store completed products or provide general warehouse refrigeration.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Equipment directly used in qualifying actual processing may qualify if the statutory test is met.
scenarios.inPractice: Distinguish equipment used in processing from coolers and freezers used only to preserve natural state.

title: Utilities and water
summary: Gas, electricity and water are exempt only to the extent they power or serve qualifying processing, supported by a use study or allocation. Storage and general warehouse use remain taxable.

scenarios.title: Gas and electricity for qualifying manufacturing
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable if used by a nonqualifying entity or for nonmanufacturing uses without a valid allocation method.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Gas/electricity used to power exempt manufacturing equipment may qualify subject to a predominant-use study; prepared-food equipment/storage is excluded from the listed treatment.
scenarios.inPractice: Separate processing loads from general warehouse refrigeration, offices and any cafe; document the study.

scenarios.title: Electricity for cold storage
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when used for ordinary preservation/storage of completed goods or general warehouse space.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Only the portion supported as directly related to qualifying manufacturing equipment/process may qualify under the applicable utility rule.
scenarios.inPractice: Do not treat all cold-storage electricity as manufacturing electricity where the purpose is preservation.

scenarios.title: Water and wastewater in processing
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable unless a specific statutory manufacturing/pollution-control exemption applies.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Certain equipment/property specifically installed to reduce water use, recycle/reuse wastewater or treat wastewater may qualify.
scenarios.inPractice: Apply only to identified process equipment; ordinary facility water and sanitation are not presumed exempt.

title: Ordinary business property stays taxable
summary: Ordinary business property stays taxable even inside a manufacturing facility: office items, janitorial supplies, racking, scales, forklifts, conveyors that only move or store inventory, and hand tools.

scenarios.title: Janitorial equipment and supplies
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable even when used inside a manufacturing facility if used for janitorial cleaning.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A different exemption may apply only where the item itself meets a specific manufacturing rule, not merely because the facility makes/handles food.
scenarios.inPractice: Treat general mops, floor machines and cleaning materials as taxable purchases.

scenarios.title: Office equipment and supplies
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when purchased for office operations.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A specific resale or statutory exemption may apply, but ordinary office use is not covered by the manufacturing exemption.
scenarios.inPractice: Treat the office as a taxable-use location.

scenarios.title: Forklifts and pallet jacks
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when used for intraplant movement, warehouse storage or distribution.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Only a distinct statutory exemption or direct qualifying use would change the result; ordinary food distribution is not enough.
scenarios.inPractice: Assume warehouse forklifts and pallet jacks are taxable business equipment.

scenarios.title: Warehouse conveyors
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when used to move, stage or store inventory rather than as part of actual qualifying manufacturing equipment.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A conveyor that is an integral component of a qualifying production unit may require separate analysis under the statute and rule.
scenarios.inPractice: Do not claim exemption for ordinary warehouse conveyance without showing a production role.

scenarios.title: Warehouse racking and bins
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when used to store inventory, including goods held for sale.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A separate specific exemption must apply; storage alone does not meet manufacturing criteria.
scenarios.inPractice: Treat storage racks, shelving and bins as taxable purchases.

scenarios.title: Inventory scales
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable for receiving, shipping, inventory counts or warehouse order fulfillment.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A scale directly used for qualifying production control during the manufacturing operation may require specific review.
scenarios.inPractice: Separate receiving and shipping scales from process-measurement equipment.

scenarios.title: Hand tools
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable even if used by employees in a manufacturing process.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: No broad exemption arises just from use at a manufacturing facility.
scenarios.inPractice: Treat routine hand tools as taxable.

title: Supplies and equipment that may qualify
summary: Certain items consumed in or integral to actual processing may qualify: required protective clothing and gloves, disinfectants used in processing areas, supplies needed for public-health compliance, and integrated conveyors. Using exempt equipment for nonmanufacturing purposes can trigger tax.

scenarios.title: Public-health-required supplies
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable if supplies are general janitorial/facility items or not used in actual qualifying production.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Certain property consumed in actual manufacturing/processing and necessary to comply with public-health laws may qualify.
scenarios.inPractice: Retain the specific legal or regulatory requirement and show the items are used in the processing area.

scenarios.title: Disinfectants in food-processing area
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when used for general janitorial cleaning or facility sanitation.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Certain disinfectants and supplies applied in actual food processing areas may qualify under manufacturing/public-health rules when conditions are met.
scenarios.inPractice: Tag the area, use and regulatory purpose; uses in warehouse and cafe areas may differ.

scenarios.title: Protective clothing and hairnets
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable for ordinary uniforms and general employee apparel.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Certain safety apparel/work clothing required for the manufacturing process, such as regulated hairnets or gloves, may qualify.
scenarios.inPractice: The exemption depends on required process use; separate warehouse, office and cafe clothing.

scenarios.title: Gloves and food-contact PPE
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when ordinary gloves are used for general work or cleaning.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Required protective gloves directly used in qualifying manufacturing may qualify under the manufacturing rule.
scenarios.inPractice: Document whether gloves are legally required for the processing area versus general handling or cafe service.

scenarios.title: Production-line conveyors
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable if the conveyor is merely transport between separate machines and is not an exempt component.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A conveyor integrated into one qualifying item of manufacturing equipment may qualify under narrow rule conditions.
scenarios.inPractice: Obtain equipment diagrams and vendor specifications before treating conveyors as exempt.

scenarios.title: Divergent use of manufacturing equipment
scenarios.taxableWhen: Tax due when equipment purchased under manufacturing exemption is used for nonmanufacturing purposes under divergent-use rules.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Equipment used only in qualifying manufacturing remains exempt; the rule includes a monthly use calculation and limited thresholds.
scenarios.inPractice: Track equipment use for processing versus storage and general use; get tax review before applying a divergent-use calculation.

title: Packaging supplies and containers
summary: Packaging supplies and containers are exempt only when a qualifying manufacturer uses them to package its own manufactured product for sale. A distributor or warehouse using the same items for storage or shipping pays tax.

scenarios.title: Nonreturnable packaging at manufacturer stage
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable if used by a distributor/warehouse after manufacturing ends or for general storage/shipping.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Wrapping/packaging supplies may qualify when used by a qualifying manufacturer to package its manufactured product for sale.
scenarios.inPractice: The production-stage boundary is critical; ordinary distribution wrap is not assumed exempt.

scenarios.title: Stretch wrap on finished pallets
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when used to secure finished inventory for storage or shipment by a distributor.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: May qualify as packaging when used by a qualifying manufacturer before the product is complete and to package that product for sale.
scenarios.inPractice: Stretch wrap applied after processing ends is distribution use unless the facts support a packaging exemption.

scenarios.title: Corrugated cases and cartons
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable for warehouse storage, internal movement or post-production distribution use.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Qualifying manufacturer packaging may be exempt when used as nonreturnable packaging for the manufacturer's product.
scenarios.inPractice: Document when cartons are applied and who applies them.

scenarios.title: Produce bags and liners
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when used by warehouse/store staff for handling or routine distribution.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: May qualify as direct processing/packaging supplies when used by a qualifying manufacturer under the applicable rule.
scenarios.inPractice: Keep bags used in processing distinct from bags used to pick, ship or store inventory.

scenarios.title: Pallets and crates
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable for reusable warehouse assets and internal logistics equipment.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Certain nonreturnable packaging materials used by qualifying manufacturers may be exempt; returnable containers require separate analysis.
scenarios.inPractice: Separate durable pallet-pool assets from packaging consumed with the manufacturer's product.

scenarios.title: Reusable containers
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when the container is retained and reused as business equipment or warehouse property.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A container's sale with product or qualifying manufacturer packaging use may change the result under specific facts.
scenarios.inPractice: Track returnable containers separately from consumable packaging.

scenarios.title: Labels applied after processing
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when used for price marking, store identification or distribution after the product is complete.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Labels/tags used as qualifying manufacturer packaging may be exempt when applied before transfer as part of the manufacturing stage.
scenarios.inPractice: Separate identity and traceability labels applied during processing from shelf price labels.

scenarios.title: Tape, bands and strapping
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when used for warehouse load stabilization and ordinary shipping.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: May qualify as wrapping/packaging supplies for a qualifying manufacturer packaging its product for sale.
scenarios.inPractice: Assess point of use and process stage, not the item name alone.

scenarios.title: Ice and dry ice
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when used by a distributor for storage or transport after manufacturing.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: May qualify as manufacturer packaging under Rule 3.314 in the appropriate product-packaging use.
scenarios.inPractice: Where ice is for cold-chain preservation, do not claim a packaging exemption without proof that it packages the product for sale.

scenarios.title: Food-contact film
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when used for routine warehouse handling or storage by a nonqualifying processor.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: May qualify when directly consumed in qualifying processing or as qualifying manufacturer packaging.
scenarios.inPractice: Identify the food-contact function, the stage applied, and whether it leaves with the product.

title: Delivery, shipping and handling charges
summary: Delivery, shipping and handling charges follow the items they relate to. Charges tied to taxable goods are part of the taxable sales price even if separately stated; charges tied only to exempt food follow the exempt sale; mixed orders are allocated.

scenarios.title: Shipping charges on taxable merchandise
scenarios.taxableWhen: Delivery/shipping charges connected with taxable items are generally part of taxable sales price, even if separately stated.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Charges attributable only to exempt items may be outside the taxable base subject to Comptroller allocation rules.
scenarios.inPractice: Allocate shared delivery charges reasonably between taxable and nontaxable products.

scenarios.title: Delivery charges on exempt food
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable if the same charge relates to taxable goods/services in the transaction.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Delivery charges related only to nontaxable grocery food generally follow the exempt food sale.
scenarios.inPractice: Use a documented, reasonable allocation for mixed grocery orders.

scenarios.title: Mixed taxable and exempt orders
scenarios.taxableWhen: Tax due on taxable items and the reasonably allocable taxable portion of connected delivery/handling charges.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Food-product lines and charges attributable to those lines may be excluded from taxable sales price.
scenarios.inPractice: Order data should retain line-level product taxability and a consistent shipping-allocation method.

scenarios.title: Handling fee on taxable sale
scenarios.taxableWhen: A seller's handling fee tied to taxable merchandise is generally included in sales price even if separately stated.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Charges solely tied to an exempt sale may be nontaxable under the applicable rules.
scenarios.inPractice: Check vendor invoices and customer receipts for handling charges on taxable sales.

scenarios.title: Fuel or environmental surcharge
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable when it is part of the seller's charge for taxable goods or delivery.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A true tax collected for government or distinct nontaxable service may have different treatment if separately supported.
scenarios.inPractice: Review the invoice basis; the label "environmental fee" does not decide taxability.

title: Discounts, rebates, gift cards and bad debts
summary: Discounts, rebates, gift cards and bad debts change the taxable base only in specific ways: a seller-funded discount reduces the price, a mail-in manufacturer rebate does not, and bad-debt relief follows the statutory rules.

scenarios.title: Cash discounts
scenarios.taxableWhen: Tax is calculated on the discounted price of a taxable item when the seller funds the discount.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Food products remain nontaxable; a seller-funded discount reduces taxable sales price for taxable items.
scenarios.inPractice: Configure point-of-sale discounts on taxable items at the net price.

scenarios.title: Manufacturer instant rebate
scenarios.taxableWhen: Tax base depends on whether the retailer is reimbursed by manufacturer; invoice consideration may include manufacturer-paid amount.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A retailer-funded instant checkout rebate is treated as cash discount and reduces taxable sales price.
scenarios.inPractice: Keep funding-source data to distinguish a manufacturer discount from a store discount.

scenarios.title: Mail-in manufacturer rebate
scenarios.taxableWhen: Tax is generally based on full retailer price because manufacturer pays rebate after the sale.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A later rebate does not reduce the original taxable sales price merely because customer receives money afterward.
scenarios.inPractice: Use different point-of-sale treatment for instant and mail-in rebates.

scenarios.title: Gift cards used for taxable food-service purchases
scenarios.taxableWhen: Tax is due when a gift card is redeemed for taxable goods/food service; the gift card does not exempt the sale.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Gift card issuance itself is generally not taxable; qualifying food products remain nontaxable at redemption.
scenarios.inPractice: Track meal tax by item at redemption, not at gift-card sale.

scenarios.title: Bad debts on taxable store sales
scenarios.taxableWhen: Tax previously reported on taxable sales may require adjustment only under the statutory bad-debt rules and documentation.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A qualifying retailer may claim a bad-debt credit/deduction for the eligible unpaid taxable sales tax amount.
scenarios.inPractice: Keep customer, sale, tax reported, payments, write-off and income-tax deduction records; do not net ordinary collection losses.

title: Repair, remodeling and maintenance of commercial buildings
summary: Repair, remodeling and restoration of nonresidential real property is a taxable service on the contractor's total charge, labor and materials included. Scheduled periodic maintenance labor on unbroken property is treated differently, but parts and materials remain taxable.

scenarios.title: Cold-room construction
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable construction materials/services under applicable real-property contractor rules; manufacturing status does not automatically exempt the building.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Specific qualifying equipment installed in a production environment may have a separate exemption; building structure and general refrigeration are not automatically included.
scenarios.inPractice: Do not treat a whole cold room as exempt merely because food inventory is stored there.

scenarios.title: General warehouse maintenance
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable supplies and parts remain taxable; maintenance labor may be nontaxable only under the real-property maintenance rule's periodic-work definition.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Scheduled, periodic real-property maintenance on property that is not broken is generally not taxable as a service; incorporated replacement parts/materials remain taxable.
scenarios.inPractice: Keep maintenance schedules and contracts, and split maintenance from repair calls.

scenarios.title: Commercial warehouse or plant property
scenarios.taxableWhen: Real property used as a warehouse, retail store or manufacturing facility is nonresidential real property for these rules.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Residential real-property contractor rules do not apply to ordinary commercial warehouses/plants.
scenarios.inPractice: When you are the customer rather than the contractor, identify the property and scope before reviewing invoice tax.

scenarios.title: Repair of commercial real property
scenarios.taxableWhen: Repair/remodeling of nonresidential real property is taxable on the contractor's total charge to the customer, including labor and materials.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: New construction is excluded from taxable real-property repair/remodeling service; scheduled periodic maintenance labor may also be nontaxable under separate rule.
scenarios.inPractice: A customer generally pays tax on a commercial repair invoice even when the contractor lists labor and materials separately.

scenarios.title: Commercial remodeling or restoration
scenarios.taxableWhen: Rebuilding, upgrading or replacing structure components and repairing damaged/defective parts are taxable commercial repair/remodeling services.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: New improvements/new square footage may be new construction; scheduled periodic maintenance has a separate rule.
scenarios.inPractice: Review the scope of work, not the invoice label; repainting, roofing and similar work can be taxable remodeling.

scenarios.title: Tax applies to full repair charge
scenarios.taxableWhen: For nonresidential real-property repair/remodeling, contractor collects tax on the total amount charged, not only materials.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Separately stating labor does not make commercial repair labor nontaxable.
scenarios.inPractice: Do not approve a commercial repair invoice as tax-free solely because labor is shown separately.

scenarios.title: Repair contract called maintenance
scenarios.taxableWhen: A repair to broken, damaged or defective real property is taxable even if invoice calls it “maintenance.”
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Scheduled, periodic work on property that is not broken, performed to prevent deterioration, is nontaxable as a real-property maintenance service; parts/materials remain taxable.
scenarios.inPractice: Require service tickets and a maintenance schedule to support nontaxable maintenance labor.

scenarios.title: Scheduled preventive maintenance
scenarios.taxableWhen: Parts and materials incorporated/replaced are taxable; service treatment depends on whether work is scheduled periodic maintenance on unbroken property.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Qualifying periodic real-property maintenance labor is generally nontaxable.
scenarios.inPractice: Keep the standing contract or schedule and the work order; one-off repair calls are not automatically maintenance.

scenarios.title: Building permit fees
scenarios.taxableWhen: A separately stated building permit fee paid by contractor on customer's behalf is excluded from the contractor's taxable repair/remodeling charge under Comptroller guidance.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A fee not actually paid on behalf of the customer or not separately stated may be included in the taxable charge.
scenarios.inPractice: Match the invoice fee to the permit or receipt and require that it be separately stated.

scenarios.title: Commercial real-property maintenance parts
scenarios.taxableWhen: Parts and materials incorporated into real property are taxable even when maintenance labor is nontaxable.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Only the qualifying scheduled periodic maintenance labor is nontaxable under the rule.
scenarios.inPractice: Check invoices for belts, filters, replacement parts and materials separately from the maintenance service.

title: New construction
summary: New construction labor is not taxable. Materials and certain inputs are taxed according to whether the contract is lump-sum or separated, and a mixed job carries a presumption that depends on the share of remodeling.

scenarios.title: Commercial new construction labor
scenarios.taxableWhen: Contractor construction labor for new structures, completion of unfinished structures or initial finish-out is not taxable.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Materials and taxable inputs still bear tax according to contract method.
scenarios.inPractice: Review new-build invoices separately from repair and remodeling; finish-out must be initial work, not later renovation.

scenarios.title: Lump-sum new-construction contract
scenarios.taxableWhen: Contractor pays sales/use tax on supplies, materials, equipment and taxable services when purchased; contractor generally does not collect tax from customer on lump-sum new construction charge.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Construction labor is not taxable; contractor's tax on consumed/incorporated materials is embedded in its cost rather than separately collected from customer.
scenarios.inPractice: As customer, expect no separate sales tax on a proper lump-sum new-construction charge; the contract and scope should confirm new construction.

scenarios.title: Separated new-construction contract
scenarios.taxableWhen: Contractor may charge tax on materials and certain separately identified services incorporated into the realty; construction labor is not taxable.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: New-construction labor remains nontaxable when separately stated; tax treatment of material/service lines follows the separated contract rules.
scenarios.inPractice: Review material lines and selected job services separately from construction labor.

scenarios.title: Mixed new construction and commercial remodeling
scenarios.taxableWhen: If one charge includes new construction and nonresidential remodeling and remodeling exceeds 5% of total, the total charge is presumed taxable unless the taxable portion is separately stated at transaction time.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A reasonable separately stated new-construction portion and contemporaneous supporting documents can support the nontaxable new-construction treatment.
scenarios.inPractice: Require written scope, bid sheets, a schedule of values and invoice separation before payment.

scenarios.title: New footage added to existing building
scenarios.taxableWhen: New footage is generally new construction; repair/remodeling of existing footage is taxable commercial real-property service.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Construction labor for the new footage is nontaxable as new construction.
scenarios.inPractice: Require the contractor to separate additions from renovation of existing space.

scenarios.title: Initial finish-out versus later tenant renovation
scenarios.taxableWhen: Initial finish-out of an unfinished structure is new construction; upgrading an existing finished structure is generally taxable remodeling.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Initial new-construction labor is nontaxable.
scenarios.inPractice: Construction timing, prior occupancy and scope documents matter; do not rely only on the term "tenant improvement".

title: Repair of equipment and personal property
summary: Repair of movable equipment is analyzed as tangible personal property, not as repair of the building. Qualifying manufacturing equipment may carry an exemption for eligible repair parts and services.

scenarios.title: Repair of exempt manufacturing equipment
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable if the repaired equipment/parts do not qualify or work is ordinary maintenance/storage property.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Repair parts/services may receive manufacturing treatment when the underlying equipment qualifies and rule conditions are met.
scenarios.inPractice: Tie repair scope to the documented qualifying process; do not assume every facility repair inherits that status.

scenarios.title: Real-property repair versus equipment repair
scenarios.taxableWhen: Repair to building/structure is taxable commercial real-property repair service; repair to movable equipment is analyzed under tangible-personal-property rules.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A service is not commercial real-property repair just because equipment is located in a plant.
scenarios.inPractice: Identify whether the contractor repaired the building shell, fixed realty, or movable production equipment.

scenarios.title: Repair of tangible personal property
scenarios.taxableWhen: Repair labor/parts may be taxable when the repaired item is taxable tangible personal property.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Qualifying manufacturing equipment may have a manufacturing exemption for eligible repair parts/services, subject to proof and rule conditions.
scenarios.inPractice: Obtain invoice detail separating real-property work, equipment work and manufacturing-exempt scope; the buyer must support its own specific claim.

title: Taxable services to a business
summary: Certain services to a business are taxable: data processing and software, janitorial, landscaping, pest control and security. Separately stated nontaxable components must be supported by the statute and the records.

scenarios.title: Inventory software and data processing
scenarios.taxableWhen: Taxable if purchased as taxable data-processing service or taxable software; service classification depends on billing and use.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: Nontaxable service components or statutory exclusions may apply when separately stated and documented.
scenarios.inPractice: Review software and SaaS invoices by component; inventory tracking does not become manufacturing solely because it supports operations.

scenarios.title: Janitorial service at commercial facility
scenarios.taxableWhen: Janitorial service to nonresidential real property is a taxable service; vendor charges for taxable supplies may also be taxable.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A separately identified non-taxable component may be excluded only where statute/rules allow and records support it.
scenarios.inPractice: Tax should generally appear on commercial janitorial invoices.

scenarios.title: Landscaping and lawn care at facility
scenarios.taxableWhen: Landscaping/lawn-care service to nonresidential property is taxable.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A specific statutory exception or exempt-customer status may change the result, but the buyer is an ordinary commercial buyer.
scenarios.inPractice: Review grounds-maintenance invoices for Texas tax.

scenarios.title: Pest-control service at warehouse
scenarios.taxableWhen: Exterminating/pest-control service is taxable when within the listed service category.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A non-taxable service component must be separately supported; location at a food business does not itself exempt it.
scenarios.inPractice: Expect tax on taxable commercial pest-control invoices and review tangible supplies separately.

scenarios.title: Security/alarm service at facility
scenarios.taxableWhen: Security services are generally taxable; bundled invoices may include different components.
scenarios.nontaxableWhen: A separately stated, documented nontaxable component may be treated separately under the rule.
scenarios.inPractice: Review monitoring, installation and equipment line items based on the contract and invoicing.
